section_summary.extract_value: This section discusses the theoretical implications of an integrated conceptualization of individual differences, training, and learning outcomes for skill acquisition in complex tasks. It highlights a model developed to specify learning outcomes beyond basic knowledge, focusing on self-regulation, transfer, and adaptability. The results indicate that individual differences and mastery training goals contribute to various learning outcomes, which in turn enhance performance adaptability, with self-efficacy playing a unique role in challenging tasks.
